review: The devs said they designed this game for 80-100 hours of playtime, so I guess it's a bit more fun than intended.

[h1] A great game with a great future [/h1]

Honestly I played this game too much to not recommend it. The combat is great, the maps are fun and the community is really friendly (I had maybe two toxic people in my time playing). So am I recommending this game? Yes of course, this is the greatest bang for my buck in my steam library, but I don't know if you can stick with this game for long. 
If you find the combat to be fun and want to see everything there is in this game you can spend like 120 hours to do all things which I would recommend doing, if it's really fun you can play this game for well over a thousand hours (I'm still not finished with everything). 
If it doesn't click with you in the first few hours, just refund it. Still I think everyone should at least try it, if a first person diablo set in the Warhhamer Fantasy universe sounds appealing to you: this is your dream come true. 

If you're not sure about it I will say this: try it and when you're happy with it stay for a few months and then run! You don't want to be around for as long as I am. So now let's get into the actual review part. 

[b] Why am I still here? [/b]

So to start I think it's important to know where my opinon of this game comes from, I remember when the first one came out, I was initially interested but didn't buy till I had already put around 500 hours into the second game, so I'm not a veteran of the series by any means. I played both games and overall I think the second is better. 
When I bought this game on launch I was actually still playing with two friends, it was supposed to be gap filler for when Monster Hunter Worrld came out, but then I liked this game much more and played it for the next few months and suddenly the game was celebrating it's first anniversary, I would say this was the best time to be a fan of Vermintide 2. Then Winds of Magic hit, I was among many of the early beta players. I won't say that I think the game got worse after this expansion, by any means right now it's the best it's ever been, but something changed and I will tell you what changed later: For now I will recommend this game again. Right now you probably get the most fun with it, since there are now 15 maps and not just the twelve of the main game. 

[b] The Game [/b]

Vermintide 2 is first person hack and slash set in the Warhammer Fantasy Universe. Further it's set during the End Times, so as always in this lovely universe: everything is shit, ohh and the world is ending, but not to worry Lohner has a plan. 
Lohner is an innkeeper in the small town of Übersreik (the birthplace of SIGMAR) and throughout the first game we somewhat save the city with his help: We are Victor Saltzpyre, Markus Kruber, Sienna Fuegonasus, Bardin Gorekson and the noisy elf. 
In the second game our band of heroes has left the small town of Übersreik (or better said has been captured) and made it's way towards the mountain fort of Helmgart. There the Skavenclan Fester has allied with the Rotblood Tribe of the norscan Chaosworshippers, it's now our objective to destroy their armies, leaders and equipment. And while we're at it: we also travel to the Castle of Drachenfels, where yet another Aids... uhm I mean Chaossorcerer is threatening the area. 

So as you can tell, this game has a story, which in my opinion is one of the many reasons this coop-game is superior to many of its competitors. Four out of the Five characters are exremely likeable, they're all well developed and have nice banter with each other. Fortune brought them together and it shows. Even though they insult each other a lot the contrary is true, they need each more than they know and it shows. I would recommend this game for the characters alone, but again there's also the actual gameplay. 

[b] The good [/b]

The gameplay is incredible in this game, it's a fully fleshed out combat system with many miniscule details you will learn while playing. The skillceiling is near endless and you can always get better, if this appeals to you, I again recommend buying it. 
Starting out you will play one of five characters, while you play you gradually unlock careers for each character, in total you can unlock 15 careers. All of them are similiar yet on the higher difficulties they will work different depending on which task you have to fulfil in a given career. Each character has his/her own set of weapons, all the weapons are good, there is  no s tier, they are all viable. So again this is a lot you can do and on top of that there are different tier for each weapon, grey being the worst, then green, then blue, then orange and then red. You get weapons by completing a level and getting a loot box, if you collect items on the map which make the game harder you will get a better loot box at the  end and therefore better loot, problem being, this is very random. 
The weaves system is better (but we don't talk about that). 
The main core of the combat is pushing, blocking and dodging while slashing at hordes of enemies. The enemies are all varied, there are as of now: Skaven, Chaos and Beastmen. Each Faction has a unique miniboss which you will encounter (Skaven and Chaos have two I know). There are also specials which you should snipe because they're are really dangerous and then there are elite enemies for each faction: Blackrats with spears and shields for Skaven and Chaos Warriors and Marauder for the Rotbloods (we don't talk about Beastmen). 
Add to that five Boss maps, there you can beat the Rotblood tribeleaders, the greyseer of Clan Fester, the Warlord of the Skaven and a Chaossorcerer. These maps are normal maps with the same gameplay, however there end event is a boss fight, if you bring the right careers these can be really easy, if not they will be a fair challenge. 
Again if this sounds good to you, then buy the game, it's on sale very frequently and even the normal price is pretty fair. 

[b] The Bad [/b]

So I'm not reluctant to recommend this game, I think it's good and everyone should try it, however: If you want to stay here for as long as me, you should go. This is not elitism, the developers of this game are just really bad at handling it and it hurts. New content is handled really poorly in this game, I've been saying it for a few months now: this game isn't dead, it's being starved. 
There are night maps in this game, but the only time you'll see them is around halloween, there are actually 16 free maps, but one you'll only see during the anniversary, I find this to be harmful to the game as a whole and not really something special to celebrate. The latest free content for this game were three new maps, they're are among the best maps in the whole series and they are my only hope that this game will become better. 
This also ties into dlc management, the biggest dlc (and the one which had a beta) was a disaster and it's incredible that this game is still alive, in other words this really shows how good the actual gameplay is. They don't do big dlc anymore, now you can buy cosmetics, which seems to work for them. 
I hope that in a few months I can come back here and delete these sentences, but as of today I will not. 
We might also get one new career this year but if we're being honest this is not enough content. Here's hope they add more maps and finally release the content they already have, if not I don't think this game is gonna last the three or five more years they are aiming for. 

[b] Edit 1 [/b] 

It's been two freaking days since I wrote this review and it's already outdated, I will now fullyrecommend this game for a few reasons: 
1. They announced an update for june 23 2020, this will feature new weather effects, this makes the game more replayable. 
2. The new career is coming on june 23rd, this is much sooner than anticipated and gives me hope, that we will actually get two careers this year.

If you have any  more questions feel free to ask me here or as pm. 
Happy slaying everyone.

This is actually really hard for me to write and I'm pretty upset.  I've spent a fair number of hours on this game and really enjoyed myself.  I've recommended it many times to friends because the humor is great and the combat is meaty.

Time for the big ol' but.

BUT.

They have started down the path of microtransactions and as a matter of principle I cannot support that.  Previous actual DLC offerings were great and offered a good amount of interesting additional content. Unfortunately, the last few months have seen the introduction of in-game currencies, "premium cosmetics," and now entire character classes are being individually sold after the developer specifically stated they would not lock gameplay components behind a paywall. I don't appreciate being lied to.

[h1] In A Nutshell [/h1]
Vermintide 2 is a co-op centered multiplayer first person combat game set in the Warhammer Fantasy universe, during the End Times story arc, when the Chaos Gods and all the forces of evil ally together in order to destroy the world. This is the tale of brave heroes and how they did everything they could to stop, or anyway delay, the destruction wrought by the End Times. You will impersonate one of five Heroes, each one with very distinct weapons and abilities, and fight in a series of objective-based missions along 3 Campaigns, against both Skaven and Chaos forces. This game strongly encourages cooperative teamplay and coordination, which is mandatory to beat higher tier difficulties, and can give out very high satisfaction in overwhelming extremely negative odds and developing your very own customized classes.


[h1] Gameplay Analysis [/h1]

[b] General Gameplay [/b]
Vermintide 2 inspires its gameplay formula to the cult classic Left 4 Dead, featuring objective based levels with a beginning and an end, in which players will have to face huge hordes of monsters mostly in melee combat though (unlike L4D2's mostly ranged combat), ranging from the common, weak Slaves to vicious Special units with unique abilities like the Globadier or the Blightstormer, to fearsome Boss level units like the Ratogre or the Chaos Spawn, each spawning at random times and locations during the level, even multiple times combined. 

While the objective of any level stays always the same each time you play it, variety is assured by some very good mechanics, first of all being Tomes and Grimoires, hidden, optional pick up items that will fill Potions and Healing slots to be carried, and will grant additional, better rewards at the end of a level if you manage to bring them all the way down, but in the case of Gromoires, they will reduce the maximum Health of the whole party by 25% for each you carry, so there is a high risk-reward factor in every level run you may do. The second mechanic that assures variety is the random factor: each run Specials and Bosses will spawn in different number, locations and timing, creating an endless number of possibilities as to what can happen during a run.

There are 5 characters in Vtide 2, each having 3 different sub-classes each with its own skill tree, unique weapons and abilities. Each one of them has a separate experience so you will have to develop each of them individually if you want to specialize in multiple characters. Each class has a defined role on the battlefield, for example Viktor Saltzpyre as a Ranged sub-class is an excellent anti boss and anti special, but is not very good against hordes of enemies, while Bardin Goreksson with his Ironbreaker specialization is very good against Hordes thanks to his flamethrower, but not so good against bosses. The synergy of all 4 classes on he battlefield and forming a balanced, all around party is the key to win or lose a game.

To further specialize a class, high-tier Orange class weapons have unique passive abilities called Traits, along with other passive bonuses, that grand the wielder unique abilities, for example having a chance to not consume a Bomb when thrown, or score additional damage for each consecutive hit on the same target, and many others. Re-rolling traits and passive bonuses of gear to suit your gameplay style and class focus is fundamental to create very specialized and powerful classes to fill a specific role on the field, this can be done via Crafting, by smelting not needed weapons and equipment and gaining resources to use in perfecting the weapons you need.

Differently from Vermintide 1, this game implements a Power System, which is not really well explained in-game. Power increases by 10 each character level and also plus the average power level of all your gear summed up. Having higher Power means being more effective in combat with more powerful attacks and greater range. Also, to play at higher difficulties a higher power level is required, so getting new gear all the time is very important as the Power of the gear you find increases the more runs you complete and Chests you open.


[b] Combat System [/b]
Combat in Vermintide 2 is very complex and strategic despite its fast paced nature. there is a Stamina system used for both parrying and Pushing, two fundamental mechanics used to avoid damage and stagger enemies when you are overwhelmed. Ammunition for ranged weapons is very limited and should only be used against Special enemies or Bosses, except some special weapons like the Flamethrower which is used instead against Hordes since it has unlimited ammo, but is prone to overheating. Also Magic with the Bright Wizard class has unlimited ammo, but using it too much in a brief time will cause the user to literally explode. Melee attacks are "free" and have no cost, and are divided in charged and Light, the first is slower and powerful, the latter is quick and less potent. Charged and Quick attacks may have different proprieties of Armor Penetration or Stagger, knowing each weapon's features is critical in being an effective melee fighter.

Attention to specials and quickly neutralizing them, good positioning in narrow paths during hordes, parrying, dodging, learning to kite bosses around while other teammates damage them, avoiding dangerous Patrols, combine classes abilities together effectively and in a coordinate fashion: all of this is part of this game's excellent and deep combat meta, which progressively becomes less forgiving on each difficulty, ending with the Legend difficulty where even one mistake, one unseen Special, one bad Parry can mean death and defeat for an entire party. 


[b] Content & Price [/b]
This game currently features 13 levels with 4 Difficulty levels. An average run lasts 15-30 minutes, depending on the level and difficulty, tome gathering and all of that. If you aim to finish all levels at all difficulties, it means this game could last a good amount of time, say 40-50 hours, if you want to max out all the classes and get all the unique weapons, skins, cosmetics, do all the achievements... a lot longer, say 200+ hours. It is definitely a bargain for what it costs.


[b] Balancing [/b]
Many requested and needed balance changes have by now been implemented and overall the game has a much better balance then when it released. Solid overall balance.


[b] Challenge [/b]
This game on the hardest difficulties is a serious, very serious challenge. It may require dozens of attempts and a lot of strategy to finish even one level at the hardest difficulty. 


[h1] Technical Analysis [/h1]

[b] Graphics [/b]
The general appearance of Vtide 2 is gorgeous. Brilliant, high quality textures, advanced light effects, beautiful art style and models, visceral gore during combat, the atmosphere of Warhammer fantasy exceptionally recreated. great graphics that really impress even more than the first chapter, a success in this field.


[b] Sound [/b]
Great soundtrack and sound effects, really make you feel evey blow, impact, cut, death: Excellent.


[b] Performance [/b]
Many patches improved game performance considerably and is now much better than before. Good performance.


[b] AI [/b]
Enemy AI, if we consider Specials, is pretty good, they will strike viciously and even combine forces, like Packmasters dragging you inside Hordes to kill you quicker! The normal enemies AI is basic, as expected.


[b] Bugs / Issues [/b]
Most serious bugs have by now been fixed or been addressed. Some still remain, but this is a lot better than launch.

[h1] RATING: 8.5 / 10 [/h1]

All the recent negative reviews are just people jumping on the hype train concerning the Red shell marketing tool. Don't let them put you off from buying this game with their lazy one sentence, badly informed reviews. 

This game is fantastic great fun. There have been issues at the start and there still are some bugs from time to time but FatShark has improved the game greatly over the past few months and they continue to do so. If you like a challenging 4-person progression co-op set in a medieval fantasy environment where you slaughter thousands of ratman and chaos heritics this game is definitly for you. 

I loved the first Vermintide game and I already have more hours played on the second game, and those numbers will only continue to grow. New content will be released (eventually) but there is enough here to already keep you busy for 100+ hours.

I only have a little over 5,000 hours in this game, but I feel like I have enough game play to give a fair review of it now. You can't go wrong with this game. It is still getting updates from the developers, and it's been out for quite a while. If you like 4 player co-op games you'll love this game.  

The largest problem is starting the game. The first few difficulties can be a slog, and the real fun doesn't start until champion. Open your commendation chests, and any other chests up until champion emperor chests as soon as you get them. Your item power increases from opening them, and saving them just slows your growth and ability to get to higher difficulties quickly, and get better chances for red items. 

There are currently three modes and, but only two are available without buying an additional dlc.  The ones that come with the base game are normal co-op campaigns, and the chaos wastes. The normal co-op campaigns each take about 30 minutes to finish. You will find 3 Tomes and 2 Grimoires hidden in each of these maps and getting them to the end will provide you with more xp, and better reward chests. Picking up a tome will take your med slot. you can drop them and heal if you find a med just remember to pick them up again. Grimoires reduce the teams health bars by about 31% and cannot be swapped out like a tome. You will also lose them if you get completely killed. They can be thrown if you get in a sticky spot and need more of your health bars back by equipping them and then long holding attack.  

Chaos wastes is a roguelite version of the game. There are no books in this mode, and completing one takes a little over an hour. However, you will probably get 3 of the highest tier chests for the difficulty you attempt if you make it through to the end. 2 will be highest for sure, but the third depends on maps completed and coins retrieved. You start with just the talents you've earned and white versions of the weapons you start with. You will find blue coins scattered across the maps that will let you purchase weapon upgrades, weapon exchanges, and boons. You can get some pretty crazy builds in this mode and it's a lot of fun. 

The third DLC mode, is not played much by the community and usually is looked down upon. It is only available through the purchase of the Winds of Magic DLC. It has a few unique modifiers like lightning strikes, harder armored enemies, and thorny briars spawning where you kill enemies. they can be fun but you'll probably want to have a group ready to attempt finishing those as the difficulty becomes extremely high. 

They are working on a versus mode. As of the writing of this, only an Alpha has been released. I was not able to play that and do not have any information on that mode. If you like Versus modes, like that in left 4 dead 2, that might be a bonus coming for you.

If you are a streamer, there is another sub mode that allows your viewers to vote on hazards and boons that they want to have happen in your game. It is very easy to use. At the map, just click on the twitch button and enter your twitch name. Just make sure you are host or your host has it turned on too. If a few of you are streaming, as long as the host has it on, if everyone streaming starts twitch mode the chats from each of the streamers will be able to participate in the voting of what happens. The frequency of votes and the speed in which they finish can be adjusted in your option settings. 

A few things that may help you starting out...
In the game settings there are quite a few things that are not turned on by default that can help. If you don't want the game to recommend a different hero, you can go into the network settings and tell the game not to recommend other heroes. If you are having trouble keeping track of team members, you can go into the settings and set hero outlines from "on" to "always on." If you would like to have actual numbers on your hud, you can turn on the numerical display. Also, the game has a stamina mechanic. holding block will show you your stamina in the form of shield icons. a normal hit from a normal rat can be blocked for half a shield if you are blocking it from the front in your effective block angle, but you will also block outside of that angle and block behind you as well, it just would cost a full stamina shield  to block outside of that effective front angle. Each weapon has a different cone shape for what costs half stamina to block in front of you. if you hover over the melee weapons it will show that cone in the top right corner of the box that appears. You can also push using stamina. this will cost a full stamina shield to do.  To push, hold block and tap attack. If you want to deal some damage when pushing, instead of just tapping attack while blocking, long hold your push and you will follow up the push with a melee attack. get used to dodging and blocking as they will become very necessary in the higher difficulties. 

The players in this game are usually great to work with. There will be a few bad apples. but try to be friendly and don't hog all of the supplies, and most people will be great to play with. Another small annoyance is if a host leaves, it will end your game in normal co-op campaigns. In chaos wastes it will just kick back to the start of the map you've been playing. if you do get disconnected from a game in the CHAOS WASTES, if you are quick and get back into the same game with the same character with the players you were playing with, all your boons and coins, will be restored to you upon rejoining. 

I Hope this helps in your decision to pick up the game, and maybe i'll see you in there! Happy Exterminating!

I've stumbled upon this game back when it was in the beta times from 2018 while watching a twitch streamer try it out and at that time I would never even have guessed that it had this much to offer and how much it means to me now.

From a game that was originally meant to be played for approx. 80-100 hours, this game has more creativity, beauty, lore, depth, personality, care and charm than any other live service games I've seen over the past years. It is so much more than meets the eye at first glance, this honestly is a piece of art hidden in plain sight, and all it needs.. is your attention towards it. The time you can spend with it is already insane and while you are getting used to it's flow of mechanics such as mastering a high skill ceiling combat, movesets, movement, item management, becoming a team player, taking in the enviroment and what's around you is going to test your patience. But that's a good thing. Learning is afterall more.. effective and rewarding that way. Times when you turn philosophical and ask [i] "why is this the way it is?" [/i] , [i] "what's the reason behind this?" [/i] , [i] "what is happening exactly?" [/i] becomes more frequent. That of course, is if you are curious enough. Once you start going down the rabbit hole of exploring and unraveling the many secrets, depth and insane detailing of the game you start to realise that this is a psychological mental trip with details so tiny, that some may never even be mentioned.

Characters are a really great example of how well they are built. From their history, through their personality changes and development with writing and voice acting so good, they feel like a real person who you could relate to and even feel their emotions merely by hearing their tone of voice, choice of words and their actions speaking for themselves.

Since 2018 this game has come a very long way, with both good and bad ideas, but most certainly changed for the better over the years. I have to say I'm grateful for the game not straying away from it's true path, sticking with it's style unlike many other live service games that get butchered for a quick hype, then getting stepped on soon afterwards. This genuinity immensely helps the longevity of the game since you know what to expect in an update yet still get surprised by the content itself. Of course there has been some bad executions, like the outstanding challanges of the grail knight cosmetic pack. But also impressively good moves like the Chaos Wastes.
We live and learn, right?

[u] A few additions that might be interesting: [/u]

[b] The customization of the Keep. [/b] Something like purchasing different sections of the keep (quarters, courtyard, main hub, emporium etc.) at Lohner for shillings, so these areas could be customized similarly to character cosmetics, just to give them a more tidy, cozy and more homely look with some decorations like bookshelves, carpets or fireplaces, patching up walls and roofs maybe few would open up shortcuts. Holes on the roof and walls, rags hanging everywhere has it's charm and artstyle I know, so it would remain an option to choose from.

[b] Mission tweaks. [/b] The choice for a quick play game, weekly to be private or hosted. True solo, duo, trio, regular 4 player, 5 player co-op modes. Level dependency whether you can go on a higher difficulty or not.

[b] Invasion. [/b] The ability to invade a random host as an enemy Warlord who can summon a horde on cooldown with special moves and abilities to attack, basically imagine playing as Skarrik Spinemanglr or Bödvarr Ribspreader vs the heroes. The health and damage as well as the quantity of summoned horde from the invader is based on the difficulty. Vanquishing an invader would provide a guaranteed commendation chest at the end of the level even upon defeat. Slaying all heroes as the invader grants a commendation chest. There can be only 1 invader per run. [b] An option to turn invasions on or off at mission selection. [/b]

Overall, I'm thankful for the devs to still put effort into their game and provide quality, hopefully I won't have to change my mind about this in the future. It's honest work, you're doing great.

Recommended? Absolutely.

Vermintide 2 is a tough nut to crack. It follows up on what was already the most rewarding first-person co-op experience of all time (albeit an insanely deep, poorly documented, and thus often inaccessible one.) And from there, it piles on heaps and heaps of extra material. But does it make a better game?

That extra material comes in the form of three unique subclasses for each character, each with their own passive and active abilities and talent trees, and a gear system that's a bit easier to grasp than the previous game's at the cost of being a bit less fun to min-max.

Unfortunately, a lot of that only creates the illusion of depth, because the abundance of choices narrow a great deal when you get an eye for how many of them are bugged/nonfunctional, underwhelming, or just straight up trap options. And this exists from the level of subclasses to talents all the way to individual gearing options. For example, Kerillian's less popular class options, the Shade and Handmaiden, sell you on a power fantasy of quickly elminating big targets with huge critical hits or effortlessly dancing around the fray, keeping powerful enemies at reach with your spear. But they can hardly compare to her Waystalker class, with a passive regeneration feature that can be shared with teammates, and an active ability that seeks out special enemies.

In general, it's hard to say whether some options need nerfed or others need to be dramatically scaled up.  Likely a bit of both. As it stands, some gear, some talents and some classes are so much better than their alternatives, that you'd be daft to stray from them. With talents in particular, there are so many do-nothing options that it feels like navigating the talent tree is less about coming up with a fun, unique build and more about dutifully picking the one option on each tier that isn't obviously a dud.

All of these plainly better choices pile up right now to create a metagame that deeply privileges characters with strong ranged abilities, to the point that players neglect their melee weapons and sometimes never develop the crucial blocking, dodging, and shoving skills necessary to play at higher difficulties. When your group's tanking specialist never lifts his shield because he's too busy shooting people with infinite ammo in his pistols, it's easy to long for the simpler days of the first Vermintide.

That's not to say Vermintide 2 is a bad game. Questionable extra junk aside, it's still built on top of the most satisfying melee combat system ever, and there's something to be said for being more popular, such that you can actually find players. The maps are also dramatically improved, and the matchmaking system is, while imperfect, a big leap forward from the wreck that was matchmaking in the previous game. But the game still needs a great deal of developer attention to make the most of all this extra content. If they can get the classes, talents, and gear to a point where it feels like there are meaningful choices, it will blow away its predecessor. As it stands, Vermintide 2 has the edge simply because more people are playing.

[i]Warhammer Vermintide 2[/i] is a game I'm honestly surprised I ended up playing so much of considering I found the first game boring. For anyone who didn't play that game Vermintide is a hack-and-slash [i]Left 4 Dead[/i] style of game, however it didn't have too much going for it. There weren't many levels to play, and the biggest issue in my eyes was that there really wasn't much reason to keep playing after you beat all the levels. Sure there are those who enjoy the challenge of beating the harder difficulties, but it's not for everyone, especially when the game is, frankly, pretty boring without friends. 

However, some of these issues are fixed in Vermintide 2. The improved item system adds a lot of replability as item rewards are less RNG dependent this time around, and you will always have item progression if you keep playing, completing quests, and earning yourself more item chests. This kept me in the game for awhile, far longer than I played the original, however it still got extremely boring after awhile, because at the end of the day you are playing the games few maps over and over again. There was 13 levels and almost any of them can be beaten in 20 minutes or less if you've experienced the level before. Therefore, even with harder difficulties as a challenge I ended up beating every level on the harder difficulties multiple times and it became way too much.

On the bright side, not everyone will have this issue. I have friends who love grinding the same levels to earn better gear. Another reason for grinding these levels is to rank-up your characters. Something that hurt my longevity with the game was that I really only found 1 character to be entertaining to play; however, there are 5 different characters, each with multiple class types, and 1 of them is sure to strike a chord with you. In fact, you may even enjoy multiple, and in that case you'll probably love the game!

I had fun with the game when I first played through it, and even continued to enjoy just playing on the hardest difficulties while I leveled my shade to 35, but once I hit that point it was over for me. Playing the same maps over and over again can only work for a certain period of time, and if they really want players to keep playing past this point they should try to create a better daily quest/reward system, as well as better item rewards and specific challenges; after all, it's a PvE game so nobody cares if you can complete daily challenges to get strong loot.

The core gameplay here is pretty strong, it feels great mowing through giant packs of rats, and using your special ability feels dope. The enemy classes are pretty unique and some are real challenges that require a coordinated group effort to take down. Gameplay is certainly where this game shines the most; it's the systems around it and the lack of real incentives that are its weakest characteristics.

Lastly, I would highly recommend playing with friends if you're looking to pick this one up. Straight-up, this game will be boring by yourself, and even with 2 players you probably won't have the ideal experience. I'd recommend playing with a group of 3-4 and allow yourself to get a feel for each character before choosing which to primarily play, maybe even have your whole group take turns to keep it fresh.

To Fatshark, I would say great job. Yes I have some gripes, but I ended up playing the game for about 25 hours and that says a lot. My only suggestions would be to have more levels in future games, try to improve the item system, maybe even allow item trading, and give more of an incentive to keep playing the game following completion of the campaign; increasing item power and leveling heroes is certainly an incentive, but not one that will keep the casual player murdering rats any longer than they need to. This could even be done with a more interesting achievement list as the current one is full of tasks that are extremely easy or unbearably grindy with no in-between.

This review is long, long overdue. I could simply point to the number of hours I've played this game and leave it at that, but I'll try to put in a little more effort. I've been a big fan of first-person melee games ever since Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, I've put hundreds and hundreds of hours into titles like Chivalry: Medieval Warfare over the years, so when I saw footage of Vermintide 2 back in 2018 I was immediately intrigued, despite not having played the first game. I resolved to try it out to see if it was as good as it looked. 

I vividly remember struggling a bit at first, with memorizing the map layouts and book locations, dealing with specials during hordes, figuring out the best way to defeat specific bosses, and learning the hard way that I should be wary of getting stabbed from behind by little ambient rats when I least expect it (there's always at least one). I often got frustrated, mostly with myself. Still, despite having a demanding job at the time, I persevered, and soon enough I was playing on Legend difficulty with relative ease (we now usually play on Cataclysm, albeit without taking books). This might sound a little dramatic, but I can say without exaggerating that I had many of my all-time best gaming moments while playing this game. There's just something special about forming a line or circle with your teammates, and then staying mobile as you're fighting a horde, elites (possibly a whole patrol), and a boss at the same time, all while hearing the menacing, telltale sounds of several specials approaching. You get into 'the zone', your muscle memory takes over, and you and your comrades get to experience that very satisfying, visceral sensation of power as you slaughter hundreds and hundreds of enemies while remaining mostly unscathed yourselves.

Summarized, this is a very specific sort of game, almost in its own genre, as it is both co-op and mostly melee-based. It's not going to be for everyone. You have to decide for yourself if it is something that speaks to your preferences. I got lucky in the sense that Vermintide 2 seems almost tailor-made for me, and I happened to make some very good friends while playing it - you know who you are. Fatshark are also known for their occasionally baffling, counterintuitive, or poorly implemented design choices and balance changes, so keep that in mind.
However, for these same reasons, if the game [i]does[/i] end up clicking with you, it's a completely unique and intoxicating experience, like nothing you've ever played before. That's why I would ultimately recommend that you check it out if you're on the fence, unless you already know for certain that this style of gameplay doesn't appeal to your sensibilities at all.

Warhammer: Vermintide 2 is a brutal, fast-paced, and highly satisfying co-op experience. As someone who loves both action and the Warhammer universe, this game hits all the right notes. It combines intense combat, a rich fantasy setting, and cooperative gameplay in a way that keeps you coming back for more.

The game's combat is visceral and relentless. Whether you’re cleaving through hordes of Skaven or facing off against the Chaos warriors, each swing of your weapon feels impactful. The weight of each character’s unique playstyle—from the tanky dwarf with his powerful hammer to the agile elf with her bow—is felt in every fight, and there’s a real sense of progression as you level up and unlock new abilities. The satisfaction of chaining kills and coordinating with your teammates in the heat of battle is unmatched.

The setting, of course, is fantastic for fans of Warhammer. The grimdark world is beautifully realized, and the environments are both detailed and atmospheric. You’ll traverse through ruins, forests, and desolate villages, all while facing waves of enemies in a truly immersive experience. The soundtrack adds to the intensity, creating a sense of urgency during combat and providing a fitting backdrop for the game’s dark tone.

What sets Vermintide 2 apart is its emphasis on teamwork. This isn’t a game you can breeze through alone—cooperation is key. Whether you’re coordinating attacks, defending an objective, or reviving fallen teammates, the success of your mission relies on the collective effort. It’s that sense of camaraderie that makes Vermintide 2 stand out in the crowded co-op genre.

The game does have a few issues, though. The difficulty can feel punishing at times, especially when facing the harder challenges. It can be frustrating to get wiped out by a single wave of enemies or to fail an objective just because of one mistake. Also, while the loot system and progression are solid, there’s a bit of grind required to get the best gear.

Overall, Warhammer: Vermintide 2 delivers an incredible cooperative action experience with a real sense of reward. If you enjoy intense combat, tactical gameplay, and teaming up with friends to fight back a relentless horde, this is a must-play. It’s a chaotic, thrilling ride through the Warhammer universe that leaves you wanting more.

9/10

Vermintide 2 is a first person co-op game, similar to Left 4 Dead, but set in the Warhammer fantasy universe. A team of four players must work together to save the Empire from the invading hordes of Skaven (giant rats) and Chaos (evil Humans, both living and undead).

I only started playing the first game late last year. I was always interested, but my time was taken up with other games. I was actually convinced to check it out because of how much I enjoyed the Total War Warhammer games, and I wanted to further explore the franchise. But by the time I picked it up in a Humble Bundle, there didn’t seem to be many players online, so mostly I played with bots. It was enough to see that Vermintide was a good game, but I struggled on higher difficulties because the bots were stupid.

Having now moved onto Vermintide 2 early in it’s life, the community is much more active. Players are joining my games very quickly and I’m having so much fun playing alongside people who understand what to do and are working together as a team. I haven’t encountered any annoying or toxic players so far. I’ve played one match with bots. They’re still stupid.

There are five player characters to choose from. Although each character carries both a melee and ranged weapon, Bardin the Dwarf and the Humans Markus and Victor, are more focused on melee, while Sienna the Human fire mage, and Kerillian the Wood Elf, are more focused on ranged combat.

Each character has three classes to choose from, which gives them access to different passive and activated abilities. You also earn a talent point every fifth level up to level twenty-five, allowing you to further customise your character to suit your playing style. And each different class has a different outfit, giving them a unique appearance.

I’ve mostly been playing as Kerillian so far because I like shooting enemies with her bow, especially because her arrows have penetration so you can get several kills with a single arrow. The passive ability on her Waystalker class slowly regenerates health when below 50%, and the activated ability fires several arrows that guide themselves towards enemies. Her higher level talent points will allow me to choose between increasing health regeneration, applying health regen to allies, or allow me to regenerate ammunition – which could be very useful because ammo is limited when compared to the massive numbers of enemies in each mission, and I keep running out.

I haven’t played the other characters yet, but after taking a quick glance at their skill trees, it looks like their abilities and talents are equally as useful and diverse.

The addition of Chaos means there is now a wide variety of special enemies to fight. Gutter Runners sneak around and pounce on a player when least expected. Packmasters grab a player with a hook and try to drag them into the middle of other enemies. Ratling Gunners spam bullets from miniguns, while Warpfire throwers scorch the area with green flames, and Globadiers throw grenades that create clouds of poisonous gas. Blightstormers trap players in tornadoes, Bile Trolls vomit acid which obscures your vision, and Chaos Spawns grab players with massive tentacles. Stormvermin and Chaos Warriors have heavy armour and powerful melee attacks. And some maps have unique bosses with their own special attacks.

There are currently 13 maps in the game, which feels like good value for the full purchase price. And I’m sure the developers will be planning to release several DLC expansions over the next couple of years, like they did with the first game. Its also worth pointing out that this game has no microtransactions.

There are four difficulty levels to play on, and I’d recommend starting on the lowest, because even that isn’t what I’d call “easy”. Most maps have one or two big set pieces where you’ll have to perform an objective such as activating some switches or moving some explosive barrels into position, while hordes of enemies constantly swarm you. You might fail your first few matches, but I found the difficulty curve became more manageable when I reached XP level 5 and equipped some decent gear.

Weapons and equipment have power levels which contributes to your overall character strength, and this determines how much damage your attacks will do. Higher qualities of loot will also have passive bonuses to damage, health, critical chance, revive speed, etc. Unwanted loot can be broken down into salvage, and then used to upgrade items and reroll their stats.

During a mission you’re encouraged to explore to find ammo crates, various potions – health, strength, speed, concentration (charges up your special ability) - and bombs. You can also find tomes and loot dice, which make the game a bit more difficult because they go in your health potion slot, but if you carry them to the end, you’ll earn better loot. Every victory now rewards you with at least three pieces of loot, compared to the single piece you earned in the first game.

Even though Vermintide 2 has only been out for a couple of weeks, its technical performance is fantastic. The graphical quality is impressive, particularly the animations of enemies, and the fact that when in melee combat you’ll often dismember or decapitate them. I’ve got a constant 60 FPS with most settings maxed at 1080p and I haven’t had any crashes so far. The worst bug I’ve seen is I’ve played a couple of matches where a mouse pointer was moving around my screen as I turned the mouse. Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.

Vermintide 2 is a really enjoyable game. If you like coop, and you’re a fan of either Warhammer, or just the fantasy genre in general, you should definitely pick this up. Maybe I’ll see you on the battlefield killing some rats :)

I've experienced the game through Legend difficulty. I have Kruber, Saltzpyre, and Sienna to level 17, 26, and 14 respectively. I play primarily with a small group of friends ranging from 1 to 2 people. 

Vermintide 2 is a fantastic sequel to Vermintide: End Times. It improved on almost every aspect of the first game, while bring new content. The general formula for the game has not changed, but why fix something that's not broken? 

Graphics: The game looks beautiful. The atmosphere and model designs are superb and really encompass the feel for the universe. There are some noticeable frame drops when things get dicey. However, the game quickly recovers and it rarely occurs. (9/10)

Gameplay: The core mechanics haven't changed from Vermintide: End Times. If I'm being honest, it's a great thing. I hate when games try to depart from themselves in sequels. You can find consistently paced levels and action. There are key areas where you can almost always expect a boss or horde. Otherwise, you never know what you're going to get. They've also increased the variety of monsters and bosses. This is always the number one thing I look for in sequels, variety. You will spend a lot of time mowing down monsters -- might as well have something cool and different to look at. The difficulty ramps up quickly in Champion and Legend difficulties, beware of this. It will require teamwork and coordination to complete those maps. I find a lot of people putting a huge emphasis on levels and gear for higher difficulties, I suggest communication. I've completed Champion difficult maps at level 1, just communicate. Overall, respectable improvements over the last game and I truly hope to see more in the following game. (9/10)

Overall, you shouldn't be disappointed with this game. It's a great title to own and play. If you go into any game expecting to find flaws or failure, you will find it. This game is no different from that expectation. Go into it having fun and you will get fun. If you look for every little thing that can be wrong, you will find it. Just know, there is almost nothing bad I have to say about this game. I'm getting the itch to fight just writing this -- So in fact, I'm going to go play now.

Tl;dr: 

         + Incredibly satisfying melee combat system 
         + Amazing coop game
         + High skill cap while still being easy to pick up
         + Great atmosphere / Warhammer setting

         - Crafting system and ingame progression are lacking and need refinement 
         


Long version: 

A coop melee game in which 4 players complete missions on a set number of maps. 
While some may argue that this quickly becomes repetitive, the main appeal of this game is the fact that no 2 rounds play out the same, as the game somewhat randomizes each encounter and the excellent gameplay keeps it entertaining, even after 1000+ hours. 

On the topic of gameplay, I can only stress how amazing the combat feels. 
While it is fairly easy to get into and can appear somewhat shallow at first glance, the combat offers an incredible amount of complexity and challenge, especially on higher difficulties.
It is on these higher difficulties where the mechanics really start to shine and the coop experience is best. 
The melee system is fluid and rewarding, with a high skill sceiling for hardcore players, yet also fun and intuitive for beginners. 

In terms of content, the game consists of 13 base maps, another 3 free dlc maps and several dlcs for more maps, weapons, new classes and cosmetics.
Mod support is also present, even on the Official Realm.
No dlc is truly mandatory, especially since you can play the dlc maps as long as someone in the group you're playing with owns the respective dlc pack.

Even if the game itself does not necessarily offer content to last for literal hundreds of hours, there are many ways to enjoy this game, from casual runs with random teammates, mutators like Twitch integration to truly hardcore (modded) difficulties. 

The main takeaway is that no other game comes close to how awesome the combat feels. Vermintide 2 is unique and amazing at what it does. 
Seriously, you'll never look at FPS melee mechanics the same way after having played Vermintide.

Furthermore, the game also perfectly captures the Warhammer atmosphere and feeling, bringing the grim fantasy world to life. 
Each of the 5 playable heroes is written as a unique and interesting character, giving them a distinct personality and leading to entertaining banter and a more 'immersive' experience.     

One of the few aspects which are currently lacking is the crafting system and the way progression works. 
Nearly everything is dependant on RNG as well as a bit of grind to unlock new classes and difficulties. 
The loot you obtain is mostly random, leading to frustrating moments when you cannot seem to obtain the desired item. 
Of course, this only really matters in the beginning, since even bad RNG can be overcome by just playing for quite some time. 
Nevertheless, the system in its current form is less than ideal.


Overall, Vermintide 2 builds on the excellent foundation of Vermintide 1. 
A deep combat system that keeps you hooked, paired with a rich setting and the promise of more content on the horizon make for a very enjoyable coop experience. 

If you consider youself a fan of either coop games, of Warhammer in general, or of melee action games - or all of the above - I can only recommend this game.

Let's get to the point. Vermintide 2 fun game-play is similar to Left 4 Dead but melee-focused with some magic and ranged weapons. I already have experience with L4D, Payday, WWZ, and KF1/2 so I felt right at home - Although with a different setting.

What I deeply appreciate with Vermintide 2, is the bigger emphasis on melee combat over ranged weapons as it's a bit more unique compared to the other horde-style games. The Elites/Specials (Specials in L4D) add some variance in the gameplay as you have to treat them differently than the trash mobs, for example. You have a ranged enemy that you can't reach far due to a melee weapon, so you may need to pull out your bow/gun or call out your range ally to clear the elite/s out.

There's a lot of melee and range variety that can offer everyone to use their play style available here; Crossbows hit harder but generally reloads slower, bows can fire quickly and accurately, single-shot pistols, rapid-fire repeaters, and any guns deliver great firepower but can attract the horde, etc~

There are 5 characters in-game, but each character has 4 classes (Called Careers). Which can cater as mentioned if you prefer to be more melee or range approach general play style.

Overall! Vermintide 2 is a beautiful dark game with hard-hitting melee/ranged weapons to choose from. Tons of fun play styles and customization options to discover. Additionally, you can also mod the game to support more than 4 players, all dwarves-run, etc.

The game deepens the already excellent Warhammer atmosphere. You won't know the exact year of the events, so it's not clear whether Altdorf is already burning and Archaon has reached Middenheim, but the mood of the end of the world is omnipresent and heavy. Dust falls on the ruins, doom hangs in the air, and Nurgle's gardens of loathing and decay thrive among the broken houses. The occasional cheerful song from the dwarf or the wizard Sienna teasing remark to the devoted sigmarite Victor is like a spark of hope in the darkness and, with its contrast, deepens the hopeless distress. The Warhammer lover will be delighted.
An exception would be found, however, in the form of the elf Kerillian. Yes, Warhammer elves tend to be dismissive and condescending towards other races, but there's a difference between the good-natured bickering of others and a constant stream of annoying insults that the heroine spews wherever she goes. You can put up with it for a while, but when he doesn't close his mouth even after two hundred hours and utters a hundred venomous rants during a mission, it gets on your nerves. In the end, one finds oneself actually quite glad when the elf is finally cut down by the hardened assassin.

Vermintide 2 is a sequel as it should be. The successful action core of the first one remains preserved, only a little more dynamism and rawness has been added to it, resulting from a larger number of enemies and therefore even more headless carnage. The creators have reworked the item acquisition system to some extent, eliminating much of the annoying role of randomness through simple but purposeful crafting. There were also light RPG elements, a more diverse environment that is no longer bound by a single city, and more types of enemies, as the original rats (Skaven) were joined by hordes of Norse barbarians in the service of Nurgle, and hideous armies of Beastmen. Fatshark's Vermintide 2 excels at conveying warrior euphoria.

Nineteen character options.
The ensemble of five heroes looks to have remained the same from last time, but that's only true at first glance. The latter will already reveal the welcome changes. Everyone now has a choice of 4 careers, which open up completely new possibilities and game styles.
If you want a dwarf Bardin, an indestructible ironbreaker or a possessed slayer with vision worthy of death. Depending on your own taste and mood, you can play the sorceress Sienna as a deadly fire-throwing machine or a melee fighter dressed in flame armor. Human mercenary Markus Kruber reveals the campaign as a Bretonnian warrior or a hunter with a death-sowing bow. Templar Viktor Saltzpyre also has a decent selection of characters available. My favorite character remains elf Kerillian, even though everyone hates him, especially his campaign as Shade, the servant of Malekith.

You literally have to build each character according to your imagination and choose the best combinations of skills, equipment and weapons and their respective properties.
Personally, after hundreds of hours I have mastered the legendary campaigns of all characters (which was my main goal) and I enjoyed each one.

I've read many Warhammer Fantasy books, so I have to criticize the game for one thing - it's not bloody enough. It would definitely need more second animation of death, real carnage as described in the books, just don't mess with heroes in gloves. Being torn apart by skaven, having a skull crushed by a beast, being eaten alive by a chaos monster... maybe I sound weird now, but this just belongs to Warhammer.

I may have beaten the game and have nothing to gain from it, but unless I find a successor, I'll still enjoy the carnage of Warhammer. I choose from 19 campaigns based on a random number generator.
Bigger, more predatory, rawer, more dynamic, more sophisticated, richer. In short, better. [b] 90% [/b]

I have been playing videogames since the 80s and have over 450 games on Steam... and this is my first ever review of one here.

[b]The Good [/b]

In my opinion Vermintide 2 is a brilliant example of what makes videogames great, because it builds on everything they did in the first game: the Warhammer Fantasy World (not that crap Age of Sigmar stuff that Games Workshop is trying to sell and failing), the good artwork, the fantastic first person melee gameplay, the cooperative nature of an enclosed goals oriented map full of swarms of enemies... Everything has been improved!

- When we had 13 maps inside one city (Ubersreik) in Vermintide 1 Vanilla and only a pair of outdoors maps now we have a great variety of locales, from the Helmgart city to the Farms, swamps infested with chaos to fallen dwarven holds...
- From having a dozen types of enemies and 1 mini-boss (the ogre rat) to more than doubling the variety with the addition of Chaos Northlanders, 3 more mini-bosses and adding real Boss fights, 4 of them.
- Respecting the story of the first game our 5 heroes go on, but now they not only choose melee weapon, ranged weapon, and 3 other items to adventure into the game, but they also got each of them 3 Careers that make sense in the Lore of the game to choose from, with passive abilities and one active ability and each with it's own Talent Tree to personalize it even more. From 4 playstyles (Kruber and Bardin were pretty much the same in V1) now we have 15!
- Keeps the great dialogue and banter between the heroes and even increasing from 20.000 lines (and by the way, that's a BioWare level amount of voiced lines right there) in V1 to 30.000 lines in V2. After playing for hundreds of hours you still find good lines to laugh about between them and makes you love the game even more.
- All of the weapons of the first game and even more were added, not waiting for DLCs to introduce them. Any other studio would have kept fan favourites locked for a nice check after launch, but not Fatshark.
- Speaking of Fatshark.,.. a small indie studio going from a small love project into a semi-AAA endeavor in just 3 years and releasing a game 3 times bigger without compromising the vision. They wanted to make the best cooperative first person melee combat game they could and they sticked to their guns. In a world full of PVP competitive games, MOBAs, BattleRoyales and shooters it would be easy to go that way to increase benefits but Fatshark said no, because they wanted to make the best coop game possible and not expend resources in an already bloated sector. I can't thank them enough.

[b]The Bad [/b]

Vermintide 2 isn't perfect nor it's trying to be, It's a niche experience, a really intense one and sometimes that can be detrimental to the fun you can have in the game because of some shortcomings.

- Crafting or customizing or maxing out your own gear suffers from RNGitis and you depend on Green Dust that you only get when you perform badly. To be honest, I think V1 had better randomizing and improving of properties/traits than 2...
[b]Edit: FIXED[/b] Patch 1.1 Gave us a way to transform Dusts and this problem has been fixed.
- We shouldn't get so many repeated Red items or there should be a check to click on to deactivate that option. It is already hard enough getting reds and cosmetics... having 5 red weapons and all being the same type is a terrible design decision, especially when in Vermintide 1 you already had coded that you can't get more than one red item.
- Too much ranged. They tried giving you more career options and they work pretty well on casual players, but when you get to the cream of the playerbase and you have optimized builds of gear and talents you can get things to be very "RANGEDTIDE". They already nerfed twice the worse offender, the Beam Staff of Sienna, that could solo hordes in chokepoints and left the other 3 teammates playing cards meanwhile, but we still have Waystalkers, Bounty Hunters and Huntsmans never running out of ammo meanwhile they kill everything in sight. I think they should nerf the ammo recovery mechanics a little to force people into melee more.
- Because Ranged is so good melee is relegated to killing heavy armored stuff and that makes some horde clearing melee weapons dissapear. Everyone is running versatile weapons that can go through armor and I know for a fact people dislike this. It doesn't make sense that Kruber, an old greatswordman of the Empire, never uses his signature weapon because it is pretty much terrible against the high amounts of armored foes running around the maps and bosses.
- Too many armored enemies. I think they should have added more "meatshield" enemies so the balance in weapons could be 50/50 Meat/Armor. The way it's working now it's 25/75 or even 0/100. Enemies with lots of health that armor penetration could not kill fast enough should balance the weapon loadout.


[b]The Ugly[/b]

- The game has bugs, glitches etc The game isn't polished to perfection, and it's better that some of the last few years AAA launches (we are in 2018, we are sadly used to it by now...), but it still has ocassional crashes of hosts (losing your progression completely).

[b]Buy it if: [/b]
- You like intense and hardcore cooperative games that ask you to be paying attention.
- Like melee combat... it's pretty much the best first person combat that I have seen. This doesn't mean there isn't ranged combat, in fact there's even too much in this game...
- Like Warhammer Fantasy or dark medieval settings. There are lots of terrible fantasy games, this isn't one of them.

[b]Don't buy it if: [/b]
- You like PVP or competition. This is a cooperative experience only and the game (and most of it's community)  only cares about finishing the level, not how many frags you've got.
- You are a lone wolf type of player. If you don't think of your teammates or take care of them you won't get far, even in the easier difficulties.
- You don't like really slooooow progression once you hit "decent" gear. Getting Red items doesn't make you OP, just gives you cosmetics and perfect stats (that you can also get with orange easy to get gear). You can be playing 500 hours and you will never get the 2 weapons you want... or you can get them in one evening.

[b]TL. DR: 9/10. [/b] This game would be perfect if they kept it in beta for 6 more months, but compared to the first game and it's rocky launch... it was an impressive quality jump.

Pros
-Addicting and satisfying gameplay
-Encourages good teamplay. The community is "usually" friendly and non-toxic compared to most large titles. 
-Immersion (sfx, gfx, dialogue, story)
-Lots of replayability
-Many possible play styles which all feel important/useful
-Runs smoothly (other than the connection issues)
-Very fun with friends

Cons
-Frequently lose connection
-Terrible net code
-DLCs kinda suck
-Half the maps are boring or unbalanced. Most of the DLC maps are tedious. i.e. some maps take twice as long and have a significant difficulty spike despite offering the same rewards.
-Devs are veeeeery slow at updating. Cannot stress how slow. Its been 2 years since release and all we've gotten are some maps and a handful of weapons.
-This game is like 50gbs not including dlc. Fyi if you're on a monthly limit.

Overall:
I'd say only friends would make this game worth it. If you love horde pve gameplay and you're a warhammer geek then its pretty fun too. Other than that the net code can be frustrating and the DLCs aren't worth it. The base content should keep you occupied for hundreds of hours if you have a desire to min/max and grind for perfect runs on higher difficulties.

UPDATE: Chaos wastes and the new heroes are super fun. You'll have to shell out some more $$$ to enjoy this but personally I think it's worth it if you already own the base game.

[b]Even after 1,700 hours, I still keep coming back to this game.[/b]

Is there 1,700 hours of content in this game alone? No. That's the magic of Vermintide II. You can come back without a fabricated goal, and without an item to grind. There is nothing holding me back from finding another game to play. Anything you could want from Left 4 Deadesques with friends is here.

The best part about Warhammer: Vermintide II is simply in-depth and how generally enjoyful this game is. There is nothing as satisfying as playing with friends, community members, or even by yourself and seeing a full picture come into frame.

There are many ways to play Warhammer: Vermintide II including whacky mods, teeth-grinding difficulty, and relaxed missions. [u] I do not recommend playing alone in pubs. This isn't about quality of players, etc. If you're having connection issues in a peer-to-peer cooperative game, host your own games. For the sake of your own sanity, don't entrust your connection to strangers. You're basically asking for a network error if you play pubs. Host your own games, please.[/u] Alternatively, play with people you trust. 

There isn't a need to talk about weapon balance; it's pretty on-point. The system has its ups and downs, but as much as I play every character, I'm still finding ways to enjoy each one with their own arsenals to choose from. I think the system as a whole is diverse to keep oneself entertained. Everything has a use; everything can be used.

Words can't express how wistful it feels to put time into a game and see results; nothing feels like this game does. I believe this is the most valuable rooting Warhammer: Vermintide II has going for it. The mechanical skill and tech is great to master on an individual level, but is even more masterable, and more perfectable as a team. There is a plethora of modded and non-modded resources to aid you as you progress in difficulty and build your skills. I'm still building my knowledge of mechanics and enemy AI.

[u]I had no idea what I was getting into during March of 2018, but I regret not a single moment of it. This is probably the best $26.99 USD I've spent for any product ever. The future is bright, and the community is great.[/u]

TL:DR - Left 4 Dead, but way better. Buy it.  (This was my review for the first game, the second game shares all the strengths, but is very much improved on the original idea.)

I'll keep this simple; this game has the same core mechanic as Left 4 Dead. It's a four-player co-op horde survival game. Except; this game is WAY better than L4D or L4D2: 

It has a much richer universe, first off, i.e. Warhammer. 

It has a loot mechanic, and I find myself striving to acquire higher tiers of loot with different item modifiers that can push me a little further. (A chance for shots to penetrate the target and hit the next, a chance to gain increased attack speed for a duration, everytime a healing item is used on an ally 80% of your health is restored, and MANY more modifiers exist.)

It has melee, variable speeds with different weapons, power attacks, and blocking. 

It has interesting missions, a story to tell, and GREAT voice acting. There is banter between the characters as they fight for their lives. 

It's polished, the matchmaking WORKS, it has flawless servers, in-game friends lists for joining/inviting to games. 

The graphics are gorgeous. 

I highly recommend this game for anyone who enjoyed Left 4 Dead.
Buy this instead of Darktide if you need a WH horde slayer. This is everything and more compared to darktide

I have indulged this game with countless hours and dedication and I can say with certainty that it is by far the best cooperative, PvE and First person melee game I have ever played. There is just as much mechanics to all the different weapons, classes/playstyles as there is a need for personal progression. If you are a person who doesn't give up and continue to challenge yourself with your party and the enemy, it is a must have. But if you think that just because you have a "powerful" weapon "you should win" then don't bother. 

It is very team orientated so if you stray too far, then you might get some nasty surprises lurking around each corner. Be attentive, listen and you might survive. But mostly importantly have patience towards all players, no matter your skill level. We've all been there, the Noob phase! Have fun and enjoy slaying hordes of enemies and make it out alive together! The mechanics may seem easy at first but the combination of different enemies it throws at you, and the subtle differences in weapons, it never ceases to amaze. There is no greater feeling than to finally complete a challenge that you or the game  has set you. Two thumbs up! Keep up the work Fatshark!
I wonder if Fatshark would ever consider adding a Versus gamemode like that in Left 4 Dead where someone gets to play the gutter runners, rat ogres, chaos knights etc. that would be dope.
